The Edgeworth Box and Competitive Equilibrium

The box holds everything two people own. Endowments, offer curves, and the contract curve all appear in one picture.

The contract curve collects points where neither person can do better without hurting the other. At the equilibrium price, one budget line touches both indifference curves at once. That tangency is the competitive equilibrium. The thick part of the curve is the core, which no one can block.

For example, say you hold 7 🍎 apples and 3 🍌 bananas. Your 🧑 friend holds 7 bananas and 3 apples. You like bananas more, and your friend likes apples more. Trading makes both of you happier. When no trade helps anymore, you land on a point of the contract curve.
